title: Count Number of Special Subsequences
summary: Determine the count of unique subsequences in an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s that follow a specific order (positive number of 0s, followed by 1s, then 2s).
statement: Determine the count of unique subsequences in an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s that follow a specific order (positive number of 0s, followed by 1s, then 2s). The result is given modulo 10^9 + 7. A subsequence is formed by removing elements while maintaining the original order. Different subsequences are identified by the indices of the elements chosen.
constraints: nums has 1 through 100000 values, each 0, 1, or 2.
A special subsequence contains a positive number of zeros, then a positive number of ones, then a positive number of twos.
Different selected index sets count separately; return the count modulo 1000000007.
hints: Track counts of valid prefixes ending in the zero, one, and two phases.
A matching new value can be skipped or appended, doubling its phase count; it can also start/extend from the preceding phase.
On 0: z=2z+1; on 1: o=2o+z; on 2: t=2t+o, always modulo M.
The two doubled choices partition subsequences by excluding or including the new index, while the added predecessor count represents every legal phase transition exactly once.
editorial: The two doubled choices partition subsequences by excluding or including the new index, while the added predecessor count represents every legal phase transition exactly once.

tests.explanation: Choose the zero and one, then either two alone or both twos, giving three subsequences.
No one occurs after the zeros, so no special subsequence exists.
